page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-2 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 7.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz, this instance allocates one physical core with two threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The x86_64 architecture includes advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), alongside a substantial 260 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2081.0 and high single-threaded compression throughput, reaching 34.12 GB/sec in gzip tests. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth performance are limited. The stress-ng multi-core metric is weak at 1888.09, and uncached memory read bandwidth drops to 15.64 GB/sec, reflecting the constraints of a dual-vCPU configuration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-standard-2 provides dedicated compute resources and modern instruction sets at a low entry point, though resource density is low. It is best suited for single-threaded applications, lightweight text processing, and small-scale background workers that benefit from dedicated CPU execution without requiring high memory bandwidth or local storage.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-2 is an entry-level, compute-focused instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs and 7.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor at 2.3 GHz, it delivers strong single-core performance, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2081.0 and high single-threaded compression speeds. However, its dual-vCPU configuration and 3.5 GB of memory per core limit its multi-threaded and memory-intensive capabilities, with uncached memory read bandwidth reaching only 15.64 GB/sec. Lacking local storage and GPUs, this instance is highly specialized. It offers a cost-effective entry point for workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation and advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX, but is constrained by its low resource density. The c4-standard-2 is best suited for single-threaded tasks, lightweight text processing, and basic background utility services.
